name: Popping
notes: Popping style pack (Doc 04 template). Funk styles, Fresno lineage: created in the late 1970s by Boogaloo Sam of the Electric Boogaloos, on Bay Area funk roots. Respect architecture: popping is POPPING — not 'breakdance'; the funk styles stand on their own and the pack says so in curriculum. The hit (pop) is the atom: contract-and-RELAX on the beat, taught before any illusion vocabulary. Related styles carried inside the funk-styles umbrella keep their own lineage credits (the robot predates popping; waving, tutting and gliding each have their own history). No knee drops or splits in v1 — those wait for readiness gates and in-person coaching.

seasons.finale: Film 8 counts of clean hits to a funk track — contract, release, ON the beat, face relaxed.
Film the Fresno in all four directions, hits landing exactly as the weight arrives.
Film an arm wave crossing the chest into a body wave, then an 8-count of right-angle tuts.
Film 8 counts alternating smooth motion and dead-stop dime stops — no bounce in the stops.
Film a 60-second popping freestyle to a funk track you've never heard. Hits on beat throughout.

attributes.name: Isolation control L1
attributes.test: 60s of alternating forearm hits — clean contraction, FULL relax between, shoulders and face quiet

attributes.name: Isolation control L2
attributes.test: 60s layering forearm + chest + leg hits together on the beat, releasing completely between hits

attributes.name: Hit stamina L1
attributes.test: hit every beat through one full funk track without the hits shrinking

nodes.name: Funk time — the beat you hit
checkpoints: popping lives on funk: Parliament, Zapp, Cameo, boogie and G-funk
the hit lands ON the beat — the music pops you
count 8s and find the ONE before you pop a single muscle

nodes.name: Texture: hitting, dime stops, and holding back
checkpoints: not every beat needs a hit — space makes the hits land harder
a dime stop is silence; a hit is a drum — mix them like a drummer would

nodes.name: Fresno, Boogaloo Sam, and the Electric Boogaloos
checkpoints: popping was created in Fresno, California in the late 1970s by Boogaloo Sam, who founded the Electric Boogaloos
popping is popping — it is NOT 'breakdance'; the funk styles are their own tradition, born to funk, not breakbeats
saying the style's real name and lineage is part of dancing it

nodes.name: The funk-styles family — each with its own lineage
checkpoints: the robot PREDATES popping — Charles 'Robot' Washington's LA scene made robotics a dance before Fresno popped
waving, tutting, animation, strobing and gliding are related styles, not 'popping moves' — poppers carry them with credit
boogaloo is Sam's rolling, loose style — it named the crew

nodes.name: Jams, judges, and the OG circle
checkpoints: funk-styles battles (Juste Debout and the jams) are judged by lineage holders — fundamentals and funk first
watch full battles: how much of a round is just clean hits on time
enter the circle to share, not only to win

nodes.name: The hit (the pop)
nodes.anchor: the atom of popping — everything else is decoration
checkpoints: contract forearms, chest and legs together for a split second — then RELEASE completely
the relax is half the move; tension that lingers kills the pop
hit ON the beat, not near it
face stays cool — the body pops, the dancer doesn't strain
mistakes: holding tension after the hit
shoulders riding up with every pop
hitting with the arms only — no chest, no legs

nodes.name: Leg pops & knee hits
checkpoints: quads fire, knees snap back a few degrees — never hyperextend hard
leg hits carry the beat when the arms are busy
weight stays balanced so the hit doesn't buckle you
mistakes: slamming the knees straight to the point of pain

nodes.name: The Fresno
nodes.origin: Boogaloo Sam, Electric Boogaloos — the first drill every popper learns, named for the city
nodes.anchor: days to learn, years to make heavy
checkpoints: weight shifts side to side; the hit lands exactly as the weight arrives
the pointing arm extends WITH the hit, not after it
rotate through the four directions without losing the beat
hits stay the same size on the tired side
mistakes: stepping between hits instead of shifting weight
the arm arriving late — hit and arm are one event

nodes.name: Chest pops
checkpoints: chest lifts and releases as its own instrument — hips stay quiet
layer chest over the Fresno without either shrinking
inhale is not the pop — muscle is
mistakes: popping the chest by gasping air
the whole torso lurching instead of the chest isolating

nodes.name: Boogaloo rolls
nodes.origin: Boogaloo Sam — the rolling, loose style that named the Electric Boogaloos
checkpoints: hips and chest draw circles, not corners — boogaloo is round where popping is sharp
roll THROUGH a hit: circle, pop, keep the circle alive
knees ride the groove the whole time
mistakes: stiff squares where circles should be
stopping the roll to pop instead of popping inside the roll

nodes.name: Boogaloo walkouts
checkpoints: travel by rolling the hips over each step — the walk is part of the dance
arrive somewhere: a walkout ends in a hit or a pose
old-man style: loose knees, heavy groove, zero rush

nodes.name: Arm wave
nodes.origin: waving grew inside the funk styles — its own thread of the Bay Area and LA scenes
checkpoints: a point of energy travels: fingertips → knuckles → wrist → elbow → shoulder → across the chest → out the other arm
only the joint the wave is AT moves — everything ahead and behind stays still
slow is the teacher; speed is a costume you add later
mistakes: flapping the whole arm like a ribbon
skipping the shoulder — the wave dies at the elbow

nodes.name: Body wave
checkpoints: head → chest → hips → knees, one station at a time
send it down AND back up
the wave has a size — pick it and keep it consistent
mistakes: bowing instead of waving — the wave is segments, not a fold

nodes.name: Tutting frames
nodes.origin: inspired by Egyptian iconography — 'King Tut' style raised within the funk-styles scene
checkpoints: every angle is 90° — wrists, elbows, fingers; the geometry IS the move
click between frames: move, land, hold; no drifting
frame the face — tutting is a picture the audience reads
mistakes: soft 70°-ish angles
floating between positions instead of clicking

nodes.name: Boxes & switches
checkpoints: build a box with both hands, then rotate it plane by plane
switch leading hands without the box collapsing
keep it on beat — tuts are rhythm, not just shapes

nodes.name: Dime stops
nodes.origin: from the robot tradition — Charles 'Robot' Washington's LA scene, made famous on Soul Train, predating popping itself
checkpoints: move smooth, then stop DEAD — on a dime, zero bounce-back
the stop is total: eyes, fingers, breath held for the beat
contrast is the illusion — the smoother the motion, the harder the stop reads
mistakes: a wobble after the stop (that's a hit, not a dime stop)
slowing down before stopping — it must be a surprise

nodes.name: Botting (robot illusion)
checkpoints: one joint moves at a time; every move ends in a dime stop
head ticks and eye-line sells the machine
constant speed within each move — robots don't ease in and out
mistakes: two joints drifting at once — the illusion dies

nodes.name: Side glide
nodes.origin: the gliding/floating tradition — street dancers like Jeffrey Daniel danced the backslide on TV before 1983 made it world-famous as the 'moonwalk'
checkpoints: heel-and-toe trade: the flat foot is the weightless one — that's the whole illusion
the body stays level; no bobbing gives it away
smooth as ice, slow as you need
mistakes: putting weight on the sliding foot
looking down at the feet

nodes.name: Funk freestyle — 60 seconds, filmed
checkpoints: hits on beat the whole minute — that's the floor, not the ceiling
at least one wave, one dime stop, one boogaloo moment
watch it back: where did the funk live?

nodes.name: Take it to a circle
checkpoints: one round shared with humans — a jam, a class cypher, a party
name the style right when someone asks: popping, funk styles, Fresno
watch one OG round afterward and steal a lesson
